p4_b3.ocr: P-values marked * indicate the variable is Granger causative of the CCI at the 5% signiﬁcance level. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0120039.t005 A normalization of CCI data in reference to 1996 data [17] ended in November 2009 leading to an apparent discontinuity in the CCI data in 2009–2010 as shown in Fig 1. To determine whether our CCI data is biased by structural changes or not, we conduct as Structural Change test [29]. The results are summarized in Table 6; the null-hypothesis that no structural change occurred must be rejected. In other words, the results indicate a structural change is likely to have occurred in November 2009 possibly because of the use of new survey or normalization methods [17]. As indicated in Table 6, all three tests imply there is a structural change in the time series, which may have resulted from the NBSC standardization in November 2009. We therefore add dummy variable D to all the independent variables of our model, where the first time period comprises 47 months and the second time period comprises 42 months.
